steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: Finance cannot reconcile instance uptime. A metered machine in an account dedicated to one customer belongs to that customer regardless of which customer its tags name, including when they name none. A shared-account machine may belong to several customers and its uptime must be divided evenly among tenants genuinely onboarded for that account; unknown or unplaceable usage stays off the bill. The onboarding records in the metering bucket beside the account list identify billable customers. Update the metering sweep so published uptime follows those rules. This task includes a local AWS-compatible emulator at the preconfigured AWS_ENDPOINT_URL. Its credentials and region are already in the shell, the repository's AWS SDK clients use it, and no real AWS account is involved. You may inspect its resources while developing and testing.

steps.message:
All pre-existing lint issues; my touched files are clean. Summary of the change:

- **`src/utils/aws/s3.ts`**: added `listDocumentKeys(Bucket, Prefix)` with full pagination so collectors can enumerate the per-customer onboarding records beside the account list.
- **`src/onboarding/entities/meteringAccounts.entity.ts`**: modelled the onboarding records (`CustomerOnboardingRecord`, `CustomerAccountEnrollment` with its `dedicated` marker) plus `AccountTenancy`, and added `MeteringRegistry.loadCustomerRecords` / `resolveTenancy` / `loadTenancy`, which resolve which customers are genuinely onboarded per account and whether an account is dedicated to one of them (unreadable records are skipped, conflicting dedication claims fall back to shared).
- **`src/microservices/ec2InstanceDataGatherer/ec2InstanceDataGatherer.service.ts`**: the sweep now loads the tenancy alongside the registry and attributes each metered instance through `resolveOwners`: dedicated-account uptime goes wholly to that account's customer regardless of (or absent) `meteringCustomerId` tags, shared-account uptime is split evenly among the tagged customers actually onboarded for that account, and anything unplaceable (no tenants, no tags, or only non-onboarded names) is logged and left off the bill.
- **`src/onboarding/entities/meteringAccounts.entity.spec.ts`**: unit coverage for the tenancy resolution.

Verified against the emulator fixtures: `cus_harbor` = 3.5 increments (3 dedicated-account machines + half of the shared machine) and `cus_lattice` = 1.5 (half the shared machine + its own), with the untagged shared machine dropped; the rest of the unit suite is unchanged (only the pre-existing DNS-dependent failures remain).
